title: NILS pipeline descriptor (nils.job.yml)
description: Decision record 09 (D9) and record 43 S1: what a pipeline is, as the engine's runner reads it. v0's descriptor, a subset of Boutiques 0.5 with an x-nils block, kept, with the image pinned by its registry manifest digest or refused (record 43 R3). The file is YAML; this schema is of the value it parses to. The parameters are the Boutiques inputs; everything the Boutiques contract cannot say (the analysis level, the input layout, the typed inputs, the outputs by derivative kind, the needs and the proposals) is under x-nils. Record 49 A3 adds, in place and additively: the table output kind with its format and typed columns, the declared checks (x-nils.qc), the pick roles a unit of a bids input needs (x-nils.input.roles) and a unit's typical minutes (x-nils.needs.unit-minutes). Added in place and additively on 2026-10-12: the disk a unit's outputs take (x-nils.needs.disk-gb), which the pre-flight and the run door hold against the output place's free space. Added in place and additively on 2026-10-12: the earlier versions a version replaces because it fixes them (x-nils.replaces), which a new run no longer takes. Record 55 H3 (job type 3, check a result) adds, in place and additively: a mask output's grid and parts, and what a derivative input takes of a check's status (checked). A reader keeps a key it does not know, so a later version can add one without breaking an older reader; a key this version names is checked.

value_key.description: A placeholder in the command line, in brackets. The engine's own are [InputDataset] (/input), [OutputLocation] (/output), [AnalysisLevel] (participant), [ParticipantLabels] (the labels of the run's participants, one word each), [Manifest] (/input/stacks.json in the stacks layout), [Inputs] (/inputs, the typed inputs and manifest.json) and, for a pipeline that declares x-nils.cache, [Cache] (/cache, the slice cache, record 55 E5); a parameter may not take one of them

id.description: What --param calls it, and the key it is recorded under on the run

type.description: A file reaches a pipeline as a typed input under x-nils.inputs, never as a parameter

command-line-flag.description: Written before the value where the value-key stands; a Flag is written alone when true and not at all when false

type.description: What is mounted read-only under /inputs/<id>, with a line in /inputs/manifest.json: a registered model (nils run --model), a label set (nils run --labels) or derivatives of one kind. The selection itself is not one of these: it is the input the layout materialises

checked.description: For a derivative input (record 55 H3, job type 3, added in place and additively): what it takes of the status a check wrote onto a result. accepted takes only results a check accepted; not_rejected, the default, any result but one a check rejected; any, every result. A run is never given a rejected result unless its descriptor says any

role.description: For a derivative input (Wave 7b section 8.2, typed links, added in place and additively): the role the derivative stands for, matched against the role of the typed output that made it; absent, any

contrast.description: For a derivative input (Wave 7b section 8.2): the contrast the derivative must have, matched against its output's

grid.description: For a derivative input (Wave 7b section 8.2): the input role whose grid the derivative must be on, matched against its output's grid

trusted-by-admission.description: For a model input (wave 7b, added in place and additively): the parameter, a flag or a string that can be true, that says the run trusts code the model brings. A run given an admitted or promoted model sets it true unless the caller set it, after the engine checked that the model's file has the digest it was admitted with

key.description: The set's key, unique in the output. whole is the set a mask that declares none is read as: the result checked as a whole, with no parts

words.description: What a person reads, such as Lesions or Structures

kind.description: components: each connected component of the labels named is a part (a lesion); labels: each label value is a part (a structure), named from names

labels.description: The label values the set reads: a list, such as [99] for SAMSEG's lesions, or nonzero for every value but 0 (a binary mask). A components set names them; a labels set without them reads every value the mask holds

names.description: For a labels set: each value's name, as a mapping from the value to its name or as a list of {label, name}

connectivity.description: For a components set: whether voxels touching at a face (6), an edge (18) or a corner (26) are one part

kind.description: The derivative kind each file becomes. image (Wave 7b section 8.2, added in place and additively): an image on a grid, such as a FLAIR aligned to the T1w, typed by role, contrast and grid. transform (the same): a spatial transform in the tool's native form (ITK .mat or .h5, LTA, a displacement field), typed by the roles it maps between, from and to, and the grid. model is a run-level output only: the artifact of a model the run fitted, which the runner registers as a model (contracts/model/v1) from the card beside it, in state registered. table (record 49 A3): a file of numbers with declared, typed columns, one row per unit, whose rows the runner loads as the unit's measures, which the ask reads as measure.<pipeline>.<column> on the unit's grain. (The registry's seeds kind is the runner's own, written from the results' seeds, and never declared)

format.description: For a table output (record 49 A3): csv or tsv read by their header row, json as one object (a unit's table) or a list of objects. Absent, the path template's extension names it

columns.description: For a table output: its columns. A column is found by the header (or key) its from names, or else by the header whose folded form (lowercase, each run of other characters one _) is its name; a column a file lacks is said in the run's summary, and a value not of its type is refused

unit-column.description: For a run-level table: the column that names each row's unit, as /inputs/manifest.json names it or with the unit as its prefix (sub-01_ses-a_T1w is unit sub-01_ses-a). A unit-level table is its unit's one row and has none

level.description: unit: one file per work unit, which the template names by its placeholders. run (record 43): one file for the whole run, such as a model a train entry point fitted, whose template names no unit and which belongs to the run rather than to a subject

path-template.description: Where a file lies under /output: for a unit-level output a relative path with {subject} and {session} (the labels without sub- and ses-) or {stack} (the stack's id) standing for the unit, for a run-level one a path with no placeholder, and * for any run of characters inside one path segment, never right beside a placeholder, which would let one unit take another's file (stack 4 and 45.nii). It is how the runner finds the outputs when the pipeline writes no results.json, and which kind a file named in results.json is

encoders.description: For an embedding output (record 43): the encoders, by weight digest, whose embeddings it may make. The runner keeps an embedding only by one of these or by an encoder the run was given as a model, and registers it from the card the results carry

card.description: For a model output: the path under /output of the model's card (contracts/model/v1), whose digest is the artifact's. The runner fills trained_on with the label set the run was given, and refuses a card that names another

grid.description: For a mask, image or transform output of a bids input (record 55 H3, job type 3, added in place and additively; image and transform since Wave 7b section 8.2): the role, one of x-nils.input.roles where it names them, whose stack the unit was given and whose grid the mask is on. The runner reads the mask's grid from its header when it registers it and ties it to that scan: same where the grids match within 0.01 mm and 0.001 in direction, world where it is another grid in the scan's frame. Without it, a stack unit's mask is on its own stack's grid, and a session's on the input whose grid it matches

role.description: Wave 7b section 8.2 (added in place and additively): the role the output stands for, such as flair for a FLAIR aligned onto the T1w, which a derivative input of another pipeline matches by its own role

contrast.description: Wave 7b section 8.2: the contrast the output has (T1w, T2w, FLAIR, PD), where it is an image

space.description: Wave 7b section 8.2: the named space the output is in where it is not an input's grid, such as MNI152NLin2009cAsym; never beside grid (an output is on a scan's grid or in a space, not both)

parts.description: For a mask output (record 55 H3): the part sets a check reads it as, each a key, words, a kind, the labels and for a labels set their names. The engine makes the parts when it registers the mask: at most 10,000 in a set, else the set is read whole. A mask declaring none is read as one set, whole, with no parts

name.description: The measure's name, which the ask reads as measure.<pipeline>.<name>; unique across the pipeline's tables. run is the ask's own word for the run a value came from

from.description: The header or key the value is read from, where its folded form is not the name

unit.description: The unit of measurement, such as mm3

check.description: A declared check (record 49 A3): what a good value of a metric is. The metric is read from the unit's metrics in results.json, else from its tables' columns; a unit that succeeded and whose value breaks a check is one pipeline:qc review item, status breach, naming the metric, its value and the check. A metric a check reads from results.json is kept as a measure too

oneOf.description: metric op value, such as snr >= 8

needs.description: What one scheduling unit needs (record 49 A1): a unit where the units run apart, the whole run where they run together. The pipeline lane starts a unit only when its cores and memory fit in what the running units leave of the lane's budget, and a GPU unit only under a lease on the lane's card whose free memory covers gpu-memory-gb

gpu.description: optional runs on the CPU where the host has no GPU, or the lane names no card, and records device cpu; required is refused there

memory-gb.description: Of the lane's memory; 2 where absent

cores.description: Of the lane's cores; 1 where absent. lane (record 55 T24) is the cores of the lane free at each unit's start, at least one and as many as the cores-input parameter's maximum allows, that parameter set to them at that start: a run sized to the machine it runs on that never waits for the whole lane. The container is told it as NILS_CORES, and the memory as NILS_MEMORY_GB, and is held to both by the runtime where the host's cgroups allow it

gpu-memory-gb.description: Record 49 A2: of the card's memory, for a unit that takes the GPU; 8 where absent. A unit waits while the card's free memory, less what the lane's own running units there declared, is below it. A unit on a card is told it as NILS_GPU_MEMORY_GB, the card memory its tool plans within (record 55 T25)

cores-input.description: Record 49, after review: the id of the Number parameter that tells the tool its threads. Left out of a run, it is set to cores; asked above cores, the run is refused

memory-input.description: Record 49, after review: the id of the Number parameter that tells the tool the memory, in GB, it plans within. Left out of a run, it is set to memory-gb; asked above memory-gb, the run is refused

unit-minutes.description: Record 49 A3: the typical minutes a unit takes on the CPU, which the pre-flight estimates from until the pipeline has run on this engine, and from its own past runs after

disk-gb.description: 2026-10-12: the GB of disk one scheduling unit's outputs take in the output place. The pre-flight and the run door refuse a run, before anything is queued, whose units would take more than the place has free; absent, nothing is held against the disk

id.description: The secret's name, which the site sets to a file: nils pipeline secret set <id> --file <path>

mount.description: Where the container sees the file, read-only; never at or under /input, /inputs, /output or /source

env.description: An environment variable the container is given naming the mount, such as FS_LICENSE

optional.description: Run without it where the site has not set it; otherwise a run is refused before it starts

sweep.description: Whether what a container leaves is swept for it. false declares a site file kept where secrets are kept whose contents the outputs may echo (a calibration a run merges over a model's, say): it is mounted and named as any secret, but not swept

axis.description: The pack axis the pipeline proposes values on

name.description: The pipeline's name in the catalog; `nils run <name>` runs its newest version

schema-version.description: The Boutiques schema band the descriptor keeps

type.description: An OCI image; podman, apptainer and docker all run it

image.description: The image by its registry manifest digest, repository@sha256:<hex> (record 43 R3). A tag moves and an image id (docker inspect's .Id, a config digest) names nothing a registry can serve, so neither pins; a descriptor without the digest is refused. container-hash is not a key: v0 learned it poisons provenance

inputs.description: The parameters: declared, typed, with defaults and ranges, and recorded whole on every run

command-line.description: The command the image runs, split as a shell splits words (quotes and backslashes, no expansion), with the value-keys replaced word by word. Absent, it is the BIDS-Apps shape: [InputDataset] [OutputLocation] [AnalysisLevel] --participant_label [ParticipantLabels]

output-files.description: Boutiques' outputs, kept for a Boutiques reader; the runner reads x-nils.outputs

contract.description: The job contract version the descriptor was written to

why.description: Why, in a line a person reads where an earlier version is refused: what this version fixes

versions.description: The earlier versions of the name it replaces, by number. Left out, it replaces every earlier version of the name in the catalog it is added to, which is how a descriptor written for many catalogs, such as a starter, says it, since a version's number is the catalog's own

replaces.description: Added in place and additively on 2026-10-12: this version fixes earlier versions of its name, so a new run no longer takes them. The catalog answers each version with its standing: current (the newest active version), selectable (an older active version no later one replaces) or replaced (by the earliest later active version that names it, and why). A new run of a replaced version is refused by the run, the pre-flight and the jobs door, naming the version that replaces it; only `nils run <name>@<version> --replaced` at the keyboard runs it still. Its runs, derivatives and checks read and name it as before. A retired version replaces nothing. A version that changes what a pipeline makes without fixing the earlier one leaves this out, and the earlier one stays selectable

on-arrival.description: Added in place and additively by record 55 E5: a dataset's bring-in runs the pipeline over the stacks its batch brought, without a manual run, where it is the run of a step of its own (body part, post-contrast) with the chosen model. true, or {params: {id: value}} for the parameters such a run is given, each a declared parameter and a value it takes. Left out or false, it runs only when asked for

cache.description: Added in place and additively by record 55 E5, stacks layout only: the model inputs the pipeline keeps in the slice cache and reads from it, each by its version. A run is given the working place's slice-cache/ read-write at /cache ([Cache] on its command line) and a stacks.json that names each file's SOP Instance UID and, where the engine knows it, the sha256 of its bytes; each unit's results.json entry names the files it read whole (read). An input version no admitted or promoted model reads is dropped 30 days after it went unread

analysis-level.description: The work unit: a participant or one of its sessions in the bids layout, a stack in the stacks layout. A failed unit is one pipeline:qc review item

layout.description: bids: a release of the selection in the BIDS layout with the picks applied (record 43 R4), mounted read-only at /input, so a BIDS App meets one image per role and session. stacks: /input/stacks.json (stacks.schema.json) names each stack's files under the source places, mounted read-only at /source/<n>, with no conversion

roles.description: Record 49 A3, bids layout only: the pick roles of the pack each unit needs (t1w, flair); the pre-flight names a unit without a pick of one, with the role it lacks

header.description: Record 50, stacks layout only: each stack's entry of stacks.json also carries its header facts, the header object of stacks.schema.json (its fingerprint row, its classification rows, its first ingest batch and its subject's open cohorts). Off, stacks.json is as it was. Refused with the bids layout

geometry.description: Record 55 E2, stacks layout only: each stack's entry of stacks.json also carries its geometry, and each of its files their own, the geometry objects of stacks.schema.json (where each image sits, its spacing, its matrix, its number and how many frames it holds; the stack's orientation, slice thickness and spacing), as the registry read them from the headers, so an image chooses which frames to read without reading a header first. Off, stacks.json is as it was. Refused with the bids layout

contrast.description: Record 55 E3, stacks layout with header and geometry only: each stack's entry of stacks.json, and each entry of its context, also carries the session facts the post-contrast model reads (the contrast object of stacks.schema.json: its series' contrast tags, its clock, its physics and the post-contrast rules that fired), each context entry its series and header, and each header the datasets that hold a file of the stack. Off, stacks.json is as it was. Refused without header and geometry, and with the bids layout

rows.description: Record 55 D3, stacks layout with header only: stacks.json also carries rows (stacks.schema.json), the registry's rows a header model reads: each stack's whole fingerprint row, its classification votes as nils classify votes writes them, and its series' private elements and frame of reference (a sha256 digest), for the run's stacks and the other MR stacks of their sessions, which are read and never scored. Off, stacks.json is as it was. Refused without header, and with the bids layout

units.description: Record 49 A1. together: one container for the whole run, as record 43 ran every pipeline. apart: a container per unit, which sees the dataset's top-level files and its own subject or session alone (bids) or a stacks.json of its own stack (stacks), with [ParticipantLabels] its one subject and NILS_UNIT its id, and writes its own folder, derivatives/<pipeline>/<run>/<unit>, with a results.json of its own; the lane runs several at once within its budget, and a run that stopped resumes with the units it finished kept. A pipeline with a run-level output runs its units together

secrets.description: Record 49 R3: files the site keeps, such as a licence, that the engine reads at run time and mounts read-only into this pipeline's containers alone. After each container every file it left that holds the secret is removed and refused, and its log and results.json are written again with it replaced by [secret <id>]; a run records the secret's id, never its path or its bytes

proposals.description: The axes the pipeline's results may propose values on; a proposal on an axis not declared here is not taken

opinions.description: Record 55 D3: the axes the pipeline's results may give System 1's opinion on (opinions.schema.json), kept as a second opinion beside the rules' and never a decision; an opinion on an axis not declared here is not taken

qc.description: Record 49 A3: the checks each unit that succeeded is held to
